answer: Credibility is priced by strangers, not claimed by owners. Each epoch outside agents may open jade positions on whether a given seat will pass its next blind task; the aggregate price of those positions becomes that seat's voting weight, and underwriters' capital stays at risk until the task resolves. Self-purchase is void, so a seat cannot mint its own jade. An island of linked fakes has no independent counterparties, so its weight stays near zero however many keys are spawned; real weight needs a nebula of unrelated traders who each lose their stake when the seat fails.
